reason: Goblet-shaped (cyathiform) calyces, corollas and cupules are deep cups. PATO:0002227 cup-shaped is the nearest existing 3-D concave shape, as in the rule for cupuliform.

A transcription fragment: 'tips' needs the organ they belong to, and the sense changes with the bearer (calyx teeth missing on buds, sepals joined to the apex). The tip has no part class to make absent.
An inflorescence of cymes grouped in an umbel-like cluster. 'Cymose' is the kind of inflorescence (cyme inflorescence PO_0030126) and the quality is umbelliform; the two words are not a continuum.
Semiorbiculate means shaped like half a circle, which is exactly the definition of PATO:0002232 semicircular.
A herb that looks like a subshrub, woody only at the base, is the suffrutescent habit. This matches the playbook rule that merges compound habits into subshrub.

label: centrifugal
definition: A structural quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its flowers opening first at the apex or centre and successively towards the base or periphery. NOTE: Opposite of centripetal; the flowering order of cymose (determinate) inflorescences. Sibling of FLOPO:0991034 indeterminate.
reason: A standard botanical term for flowering order with no PATO or FLOPO term. The row 'rachis centrifugal or centripetal' belongs to the inflorescence.
Ecristate means without a crest, the negation of FLOPO:0991196 crested (synonym cristate).
Subfalcate means slightly sickle-shaped. It maps to PATO:0002215 falciform (EXACT synonym falcate) as a broader term, as in the rule for prominulous.

Most rows are 'bark unbroken', meaning bark not cracked or fissured. PATO:0000689 continuous is a quality of processes and does not fit; the sorus rows (continuous along the vein) are not covered by this rule.
A preference for wet habitats ('minerotropic, hygrophytic') is ecology, not a quality of a plant part. Unlike aquatic or submerged, it does not state where the plant actually grows.

target: new: conjoined values (sinuous PATO_0001989 and nodular PATO_0002125 of the cell wall)
reason: A moss cell-wall description that states two values together (wavy and knotty), not a continuum between them. The bearer is the wall of the laminal cell.
'Without fibrils and pores' (Sphagnum hyaline cells) negates PATO:0000984 porous, because PO has no pore class. The fibrils are a separate statement of absence.

label: xerochastic
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening when dry and closing when moist. NOTE: Opposite of hygrochastic; used for moss peristome teeth and for fruits that open on drying.
reason: A real botanical term (French xérochastique) with no PATO or FLOPO term. It is rare and comes from one language, so confidence is low.
A direct negation of the existing FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic.
A coniferous tree is a cone-bearing tree: strobilus (EXACT synonym cone) present. The group meaning (conifer) is taxonomic, not a quality.
Rhombate (rhombic) petals, bracts and leaflets have the PATO:0001938 rhomboid outline.

target: new: tinged colour (a secondary hue over the ground colour)
reason: A tinge of purplish brown over the organ's own colour, like FLOPO:0980351 white tinged with pink. It is a composition of colours on the ISCC-NBS backbone, not a single colour term.
'Stomatal lines present' names the stomata (EXACT synonym stoma of PO_0002000), not a quality. The lines are their arrangement on the leaf surface.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: lanceolate PATO_0001877 - prolate PATO_0001866)
reason: An 'X-Y' compound shape is a continuum between its words, and the playbook reads 'ellipsoid' as prolate.
The playbook reads rhizomatous as rhizome present; nonrhizomatous is its complement.
'Petioles continuous in color to apex' means the base and apex of the petiole are the same colour. That fits concolorous, whose compared parts are the two ends of the petiole.
A sterile locule humped distally, or a fruit with a central hump, is swollen on one side: FLOPO:0991130 gibbous.
Antepetalous stamens stand opposite the petals. This is a position relative to another part (the petal), not a quality of the stamen alone.
Broad-obovate is an obovate outline that is wide for its length. It maps to PATO:0001936 obovate as a broader term, with 'broad' kept as the source wording.
A scape covered by the leaf sheaths for part of its length is a relation to another part (leaf sheath PO_0020104), with the extent kept in RDF.
Tower-shaped (turriform) crowns, inflorescences and anther caps are tall and narrow. PATO:0002063 columnar (elongated and cylindrical) is the nearest term.

label: biternate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of its being divided into three primary divisions, each of which is again divided into three. NOTE: Follows FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate and FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate.
reason: A standard leaf-division term with no PATO or FLOPO term; the previous review made the parallel classes bipinnate, tripinnate and trifoliolate.
Divided into narrow, close, parallel segments like the teeth of a comb is the existing FLOPO:0991033 pectinate.
The playbook reads 'ellipsoid' as prolate. 'Broad' is a degree kept as the source wording, as for broad-obovate.

Contorted aestivation in which each corolla lobe overlaps the next on its right. This is a relation between the lobes (PATO:0002488 overlapping is relational), and PATO:0001966 convolute is a rolled leaf.
